teaser: Jeremiah Grossman's warning about php2shell scanners, checked against what the evidence holds a day later: loud noise, a quiet signal.
core_idea: Most php2shell scanners read the version string, which cannot see a distribution's backported fix, so patched servers are reported vulnerable; the noise is already in bulk while the compromise map holds no named victim, so the false positives, and the sites switched off because of them, are an incident of their own.

quotes.text: A false positive in one scanner is a bug. A false positive sent to many people at once is noise, and it scales.
quotes.why: The noise is already in bulk.

quotes.text: The problem is that the people downstream act on the first version.
quotes.why: Detection rules fail in both directions.

quotes.text: It is an incident of its own, and it is not in anyone's breach count.
quotes.why: A quiet signal under a loud alarm.
